samples.question: The board is a plain sand-coloured surface littered with small coloured decorative marks - dots, bars, rings and squares - that mean nothing. Lying on the board are exactly three white cards with thin dark borders, all close together in one small part of the board; they never touch each other or any decorative mark, and nothing else in the picture is white. One card is clearly larger than the other two: that large card is the SEAL. The two smaller cards are the KEYS. Every one of the three cards carries, near its top, a row of exactly three short black ticks. On every card the ticks sit on the same invisible lattice of seven evenly spaced slots with the same spacing, so a tick row is fully described by the two slot gaps between its first and second tick and between its second and third tick. The seal's two gaps are never equal. Exactly one key repeats the seal's tick row SLID sideways: its two gaps, read left to right, are the seal's two gaps in the same order. The other key repeats the seal's tick row MIRRORED left to right: its two gaps, read left to right, are the seal's two gaps in the opposite order. Both keys are slid to a different starting slot from the seal's row, both carry exactly three ticks, and both carry exactly the same amount of tick ink, so ink, tick count, card size, card colour and card position tell you nothing about which key is the mirrored one. Below its tick row each key also carries a row of PIPS: between one and four small black filled squares, clearly shorter than the ticks. The two keys always carry different pip counts. The seal carries no pips. You must find the seal, compare each key's tick rhythm with the seal's, and decide which key is the mirrored one before reading its pips. How many pips does the MIRRORED key carry? Answer one, two, three or four.
